entries.title: Sources lists the links in the article
entries.body: Sources has a new Links view: every web address the article itself links to, in the order it first appears, with the author's own link words, the site it points to, and a jump to the paragraph that uses it. Where a link matches a work in the Bibliography, a button opens that entry. It is read straight from the article, so nothing is sent to the AI and nothing is fetched.

entries.title: Command bar suggestions are shorter, and dismissable
entries.body: With the command bar empty, Guide comes first and the suggestions drawn from why you're reading take at most four rows. Dismiss one with × or the Delete key and it is hidden for that article until your profile or reason for reading changes; the list's heading folds it away. Exports of the article include what you dismissed.

entries.title: Bibliography no longer repeats its not-read note
entries.body: The Bibliography list, and the card that appears when you point at a citation, used to repeat the same note on every row saying the cited work had not been read. That note appears once above the list, and only when a row it applies to is showing. Notes particular to one work stay on that work.

entries.title: Chat summaries show under Reception angles and comments
entries.body: On your own articles, when you have asked in chat from a Reception angle or from a comment, a short summary of that conversation appears beneath it, as it already did in other places. You can see what the conversation was about without opening it.

entries.title: Notes on Bible Gateway pages are recognised
entries.body: On Bible Gateway pages, lettered cross-reference markers such as (A) and footnotes such as [a] are now recognised as notes: pointing at one shows its note, and clicking takes you to it. Articles you added before this need adding again to pick up the fix.

entries.title: A lone margin note is no longer lost
entries.body: When an article had a single side note in its margin with no separate label, that note's text was lost when the article was added. It is kept, and linked to the passage it belongs to.
